question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-4x(t)+4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[1,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[-1,\text{ }2]^{T},$ respectively. Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
question.worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Let's now sketch the phase portrait.

- First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/033fb4b6f35c06e8d718df9b8e88d47b7461f247121f1e859c6fba41cfda9112.png)

- Now, the line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 
$y=-2x$
and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. Since ${e}^{6t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/eabc6882089c4e26e497b8adae004018e132874dd9e02d33caeddd3967330c87.png)

All other non-equilibrium solutions are parallel to the vector ${v}_{2}.$ So, the phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/868becabde44fa1173fcf0a41424bfcad678a03f5449f62706a7f814563347dc.png)
